tools.name: mcp__upwork__upwork__boost_profile
tools.description:
Despite the name, this tool CANNOT start or increase a profile boost or the availability badge (PIB). It only reads their status and stops, pauses or switches off ones already running. Starting or increasing ad spend is done on upwork.com, not here.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
Returns a preview — call confirm_preview only after explicit user approval.

Actions:
- get_status: Read current state of visibility boosters: availability badge (on/off, weekly Connects budget, cost) and profile boost ad (status, bid, targeting). No params required.
- toggle_availability_badge: Switch OFF the Availability Badge (Available Now). Enabling it is done on upwork.com — it starts a RECURRING WEEKLY Connects charge, so it is not set up on the user's behalf here. Calling with enabled=true returns the link to set it up. Params: enabled (bool, required — false turns the badge off).
- create_profile_boost: NOT AVAILABLE HERE — profile boost ads are created on upwork.com. A boost bid is an amount you choose for advertising, so it is not set up on the user's behalf through this tool. Calling this returns the link to set it up. Use get_status to read an existing ad, and manage_profile_boost to stop or pause one. Takes no params.
- manage_profile_boost: Stop or pause an existing profile boost ad. Restart and update are done on upwork.com: both increase spend, so they are not performed on the user's behalf here. Params: action (string, required — stop or pause; restart and update return the link to upwork.com instead), ad_id (string, required).

tools.name: mcp__upwork__upwork__confirm_attachment_upload
tools.description:
Confirm uploaded files so they are retained in Upwork storage. Applies to fallback messages, offer and milestones uploads: job, proposals and invitation uploads are retained during upload (confirming them has no effect). Permanent: confirmed files are kept and cannot be un-confirmed or deleted through this API; re-confirming is a no-op. Requires the upload context and the file_uid values returned from upload.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.

Actions:
- confirm: Params: file_ids (array of strings, required — file_uid values to confirm); task_id (string, required — the task_id returned by start_attachment_upload for these files); context (string, optional — taken from the upload session; if given it must name the same backend the session was started with, or the call is refused). Only file_uid values that get_upload_status reports as done for that task_id can be confirmed; anything else is refused. Upload sessions last 30 minutes, so confirm promptly. Files uploaded through the inline component are already stored and must NOT be confirmed.

tools.name: mcp__upwork__upwork__confirm_draft
tools.description:
Deprecated alias of confirm_preview (identical behaviour) — prefer confirm_preview. For job postings specifically: calling create_draft (type='job_posting') always saves a real DRAFT — it never publishes, no matter what the action is labeled, and it leaves no preview to confirm here. To publish an existing job posting, call post_job update with status: 'published' and confirm that (type='job_update') — that step makes the job live to whoever its access level allows, opening it for proposals immediately.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.

Actions:
- confirm: Confirm and execute a preview using preview_id only. Params: type (string, required), preview_id (string, required — from the create preview response; the legacy name draft_id is also accepted). Do not pass the returned params; they are loaded from server storage.

draft_id.description: Legacy name for preview_id, accepted so clients built against the published confirm_draft metadata keep working. Send preview_id instead; if both are present, preview_id wins.

preview_id.description: Server-issued preview_id from the create preview response. Required unless the legacy draft_id is given instead. confirm_preview executes stored server params only — do not pass confirm payloads.

type.description: The entity type, from the enum. confirm_preview does NOT execute offer ACCEPTANCE (that is finalized on upwork.com via the finalize_url); offer decline and request-changes ARE supported.

tools.name: mcp__upwork__upwork__confirm_preview
tools.description:
Confirm and execute a previously prepared preview for job postings, proposals, invitation accepts, invitations, milestones, profile updates, and offer decline / request-changes. Requires preview_id from the prior preview action. Do NOT use to ACCEPT an offer — accepting is finalized on upwork.com via the finalize_url returned by respond_to_offer accept. For job postings specifically: calling create_draft (type='job_posting') always saves a real DRAFT — it never publishes, no matter what the action is labeled, and it leaves no preview to confirm here. To publish an existing job posting, call post_job update with status: 'published' and confirm that (type='job_update') — that step makes the job live to whoever its access level allows, opening it for proposals immediately.

You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.

tools.name: mcp__upwork__upwork__respond_to_offer
tools.description:
Accept, decline, or request changes to a client offer. Use this tool for all offer responses. 'decline' and 'request_changes' run through MCP (draft -> confirm_preview). 'accept' is legally binding and must be completed by you on Upwork — it returns a link. Use list_offers action=list_mine to find your offers and the offer ID.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
Returns a preview — call confirm_preview only after explicit user approval.

Actions:
- accept: Get the Upwork link to ACCEPT an offer. Accepting is legally binding (it starts the contract) and must be done by the person on Upwork — this returns a finalize_url, it does NOT accept the offer. The offer_id must come from list_offers (action=list_mine or get). Params: offer_id (string, required).
- decline: Decline an offer from a client (not binding; confirm_preview type='offer_decline'). The offer_id must come from list_offers (action=list_mine or get). Params: offer_id (string, required), reason (string, optional — one of: terms, busy, duplicate, no_response, spam, error, other, requirements), message (string, optional — message to the client).
- request_changes: Request changes to an offer / counter-offer (NOT binding — the client must approve and send an updated offer; confirm_preview type='offer_request_changes'). Params: offer_id (string, required — the offer to change), description (string, required — the changes you're requesting), hourly_rate (string, required — requested rate, e.g. '55.00'), currency (string, default USD), weekly_limit (number, optional), message (string, optional — note to the client).

tools.name: mcp__upwork__upwork__save_job
tools.description:
Manage your own marketplace job lists: save (favorite) a job to come back to it, or hide a job to keep it out of your search results. Both lists are private — the client is never notified, and hiding is not feedback about the client or a review of any kind. Hidden jobs are already excluded from future search results by the backend, so no extra filtering is needed in find_jobs. Get job_id from find_jobs (search or get). Browse saved jobs with find_saved_jobs.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.

Actions:
- save: Save a job to your saved jobs list. Params: job_id (string, required — job posting ID).
- unsave: Remove a job from your saved jobs list. Params: job_id (string, required — job posting ID).
- hide: Hide a job so it stops appearing in your search results, recording why. Params: job_id (string, required — numeric id from find_jobs), reason (string, required — one of: not_interested, vague_description, unrealistic_expectations, too_many_applicants, too_old, poor_client_reviews, doesnt_match_skills, overqualified, too_low_budget, location_mismatch). The client is not notified and cannot see this.
- unhide: Un-hide a job you previously hid, letting it appear in search results again. Params: job_id (string, required — numeric id from find_jobs).
- hide_status: Check whether you have hidden a job, and for what reason. Params: job_id (string, required — numeric id from find_jobs).

tools.name: mcp__upwork__upwork__start_attachment_upload
tools.description:
Requests a secure file upload from the user. Creates a short-lived upload session and returns task_id plus fallback_url. For messages uploads with user_id and org_id this may create or reuse a 1:1 room with that person — a connection they can see that consumes the daily new-connection limit — so never guess a recipient. Retention is per context: job, proposals and invitation uploads are retained on upload; fallback messages, offer and milestones uploads are retained only after confirm_attachment_upload. In MCP App-capable hosts, an inline upload UI may appear; otherwise share fallback_url with the user. The inline upload UI supports up to 7 MB per file. The fallback_url page supports up to 100 MB per file and 300 MB total; use it for larger files. Never ask for base64 text or local file paths. Before calling upload, you MUST know the upload context. Ask the user to choose messages, proposals, offer, milestones, job, or invitation when it is not obvious from the conversation. Never guess a context.

WRITE OPERATION — REQUIRES EXPLICIT USER CONFIRMATION.
You MUST present full action details and receive explicit approval before executing.
Actions: upload.
Call get_tool_help(tool_name="start_attachment_upload") for the parameters and how to use this tool.
